title: Postern describe response
description: Response body of GET /postern/v0/describe. See SPEC.md section 4.1.

postern.description: Specification version this payload conforms to.

id.description: Agent identifier (SPEC.md section 1.5): two parts of lowercase ASCII alphanumerics, '-' and '.', joined by one '/'. Stable, and unique within the distributor. Compared octet-for-octet; addressed as two path segments on a distributor and never percent-encoded.

inputs.description: Ordered input declarations. An envelope: the specification fixes the shape of the list, not how an agent arrives at its contents.

type.description: The output types a conforming implementation emits. text is prose; bytes is a file, and value then carries it base64-encoded (SPEC.md section 4.1.4) — value is a JSON string either way. A client MUST NOT use this enum to reject a response — and unlike every other unknown in this protocol, an unrecognised output type may not simply be ignored either: a client MUST NOT present value as text, MUST NOT report the run as failed, and SHOULD say which type it was given.

media_type.description: An RFC 6838 media type naming what value carries. REQUIRED when type is bytes, and meaningless otherwise. Open rather than an enum on purpose: closing it would need a specification revision per format. The pattern is RFC 6838 section 4.2's restricted-name for both parts, lowercased: a runner emits lower case so that two runners naming one format agree octet-for-octet (SPEC.md section 4.1.4). A client MUST NOT reject a response for the case of this field — media types are case-insensitive (RFC 9110), and these schemas describe what a conforming runner emits, not what a client accepts.

idempotent_retry.description: Whether the runner honours an Idempotency-Key (SPEC.md section 4.2): a request carrying a key it has already answered MUST NOT execute the agent again, and is answered with the result of the first execution. A client reads absent and false identically — a retry executes again. A Level 1 runner implements no run and SHOULD NOT declare it.

tools.description: Every tool the agent can invoke.

write_tools.description: The subset of tools that spend money, mutate state outside the workspace, or are otherwise not safely repeatable. MUST be a subset of tools.

credentials.description: Credentials declared by environment variable NAME only. A value here is nonconformant.

items.description: One declared credential. Closed on purpose, and the only closed object in these schemas outside error.schema.json's root (error.code and output.type are closed enums, a different thing): SPEC.md section 4.1.3 says there is nowhere in the protocol for a secret to travel, and an open object here is somewhere - value beside env would be schema-valid, as would every other spelling of the leak that section forbids. It catches the structural half and not the whole of it, since a value written into purpose is a conforming shape carrying a nonconformant string. Like every file here this describes what a conforming runner emits, so a client MUST NOT reject a describe over a member it does not recognise (see schemas/README.md).

env.description: Environment variable name. Never a value.

purpose.description: One line on what the agent does with it. Written for a person reading a listing before they install anything; no runner reads it.

signup_url.description: Where a buyer obtains one. Same audience as purpose, and no runner reads it either.

key.description: Key used in the run request's inputs map, and the input's identifier: ASCII letters and digits, underscore, dot and hyphen, one character or more (SPEC.md section 4.1.1). A client renders it as the name of a thing - a form field, a command-line flag, a column heading - and label carries the human-facing name, so the key does not have to. Length is deliberately unbounded, unlike an agent identifier's, because a key crosses no trust boundary. The key 'prompt' is reserved for a single free-text brief.

type.description: Clients MUST treat an unrecognised type as text rather than failing.

default.description: Follows the value space of type (SPEC.md section 4.1.1): a string for text and select, a number for number, null for no value. No v0 input type produces a boolean. The allOf below enforces that pairing, which is possible here because the type and the default sit in one object; run-request.schema.json cannot, since the values there are in a different document from the declarations that type them, so it admits the union of the three value spaces and section 4.2 leaves the per-input check to the runner.

validation.description: Open object. Unrecognised members MUST be ignored, not rejected.

allOf.description: This branch and the next hold default to the value space its type declares (SPEC.md section 4.1.1). Both are keyed positively on the types they constrain, never negatively on the ones they do not: section 4.1.1 anticipates a fourth type, and a branch reading 'anything that is not number' would constrain it the moment it arrived.
